messages:
kevin: thinking out loud — propose default 'graduated-surge-mitigator' canary schedule for model version swaps.

kevin: high level idea: very small initial exposure, then graduated jumps with telemetry gates. trying to balance detection vs rollout time.

sara: +1 to smaller first step. prefer 0.5% vs 1% for noisy traffic.

amanda: we should gate on error-rate increase OR p95 latency regression > 20% (relative). also tie safety evals in.

jon: agree. add guard to block forward roll if any safety eval fails or if user-facing error rate > 0.5% (0.005).

kevin: also propose backoff: if guard trips, rollback to previous stable and pause further roll for 10m; emit alert to oncall.

sara: telemetry: ensure we emit cohort split tag and model.version in traces, and a 'canary.step' metric per request. need dashboards for p95 delta and error ratio by cohort.

kevin: console UX: show predicted traffic counts for each step + estimated cost delta and SLO risk so product owners can make informed decisions. add an optional "fast-path" toggle for low-risk infra-only models.

amanda: small config sketch: 
```
policy_name: graduated-surge-mitigator
steps:
  - pct: 0.5
    duration: 15m
  - pct: 3
    duration: 15m
  - pct: 15
    duration: 30m
  - pct: 40
    duration: 1h
  - pct: 100
    duration: 30m
guards:
  - type: error_rate
    threshold: 0.005
  - type: p95_latency_rel
    threshold: 0.20
fallback: rollback_to_previous
```

jon: canary-bot: simulate command please (need numbers to validate cadence).

canary-bot: simulated traffic profile run started for policy=graduated-surge-mitigator; estimated 14k requests in first 2h; will emit sample telemetry after run.

sara: one more ask — ability to inject random jitter to step timing ±10% to avoid synchronized rollouts across clusters. also cohort affinity so device-heavy cohorts are stable.

kevin: noted. next: I'll open a PR with config + console mocks and a telemetry dashboard proposal. tagging @sre-team @oncall for review.

amanda: SGTM :thumbsup:

jon: lgtm

kevin: thanks folks, will file follow-ups for telemetry dashboards and canary simulation job.
